title.title: The triangular Hilbert transform at the symmetric point
title.subtitle: Claim: the maximal triangular Hilbert transform is bounded $L^3 \times L^3 \to L^{3/2}$

plain: Three functions, each blind to one direction, tangled in a cycle: can their combined average blow up?

beats.text: $F$ is read at $(x+t,y)$ and $G$ at $(x,y+t)$: a right triangle for each $t$
Integrated against $dt/t$, the variables form an entangled cycle
The claim: the first Lebesgue bound of any kind for the flat operator

steps: Write the form as a trace of products of operators
Attach a nonnegative matrix 'energy' to it
Heat flow lowers that energy at a rate that bounds the form

achievement.label: Thiele's Problem 13: the exponents (3, 3, 3)
achievement.context: Before: no Lebesgue bound of any kind for the flat operator
achievement.note: Only the symmetric point; the rest of the conjectured range is not claimed

verify.detail: Lean: the maximal $L^3 \times L^3 \to L^{3/2}$ bound. Not the variation or dyadic results
verify.ourCheck: We read the review of the statement; we did not run Comparator

voice.text: Two functions on a triangle, entangled in a cycle. No bound at all was known.
A matrix energy falls under heat flow, and its fall bounds the form.
Claimed: a bound at the symmetric point.

sources.quote: Thiele's problem list (arXiv:1701.06637, Section 9 Problem 13) asks for the L^3×L^3×L^3 bound.
No Lebesgue bound for the flat operator was known before this release.
NOT formalized: annular r-variation (Oct 5) and the dyadic absolute bound.
Only the symmetric point; boundedness at other Hölder exponents (the general THT conjecture) is not claimed.
